ambiguities.description: Toby is explicitly described as ten years old in chapter 2, but as fifteen years old in chapters 9 and 10.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Do not use Toby’s exact age as retrieval ground truth until human review or later source clarification.

ambiguities.description: Gregor is explicitly described as sixty-five in chapters 2, 7, and 9, but as sixty in chapter 6.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Treat Gregor as elderly; exclude exact age from benchmark ground truth.

ambiguities.description: Alan’s continuing shoulder injury is described as left shoulder in chapter 2 and again as the left shoulder drooping in chapter 15, but it is repeatedly described as the right shoulder in chapters 3, 5, 6, and 11–19.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: The existence and persistence of the shoulder injury are canonical; exact side is excluded from ground truth.

ambiguities.description: Chapter 5 states Miller and Jory have not been found and may be deeper underground; chapter 6 has Alan report that they died on the second underground level.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Do not label their death/location as canonical in B01. Memory chunks preserve the chapter-5 uncertainty; chapter-6 death statement is treated as a conflicting report, not resolved fact.

ambiguities.description: The creatures’ corrosive secretion is alternately described using acid and alkaline terminology, and neutralization chemistry is internally inconsistent.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Use only the robust narrative fact that the secretion is highly corrosive/toxic; do not benchmark exact acid-vs-alkali chemistry.

ambiguities.description: Chapter 9 ends with defenders and villagers retreating into the council-house refuge and sealing the door after the horde breaches Oakhaven. Chapter 10 resets to a pre-assault preparation sequence; chapters 11–12 then continue that branch with a western defense and Roland’s arrival. The chapter-10+ sequence is internally progressive but its placement relative to the chapter-9 refuge ending is unresolved.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Treat chapters 10–19 as an internally ordered branch for local state changes, but do not use the chapter-9→10 transition as clean temporal ground truth until human review.

ambiguities.description: Elena’s hair is described as black in chapter 1, brown in chapter 2, and chestnut in chapter 8.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Exclude exact hair color from retrieval ground truth.

ambiguities.description: Temple extraction behavior is directly observed locally (chapter 14), and Alistair directly confirms in chapters 20–21 that he accepts sacrifice to maintain the Vòm Trời / stabilize Solaria. However, some broader technical claims about the complete siphoning chain, exact system mechanics, and all downstream effects remain only partially demonstrated.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Treat local extraction and Alistair’s stated maintenance/sacrifice objective as canonical. Keep unobserved engineering details and numerical/causal claims as attributed or inferred until directly demonstrated.

ambiguities.description: A scout named Miller is introduced as missing in chapter 3, while chapter 13 refers to an elderly blacksmith Miller and chapter 19 mentions Miller’s children. The source does not explicitly establish whether these references name the same person.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Keep the scout Miller and blacksmith Miller as separate entity IDs. Do not merge until explicit source evidence resolves identity.

ambiguities.description: The stated size/severity measurements of Alan’s persistent shoulder tear fluctuate sharply (for example, from centimeters-like “phân” descriptions to several “tấc” and back), beyond a clearly narrated healing/reinjury progression.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: The persistent and worsening shoulder injury is valid ground truth; exclude exact wound length measurements from evaluation labels.

ambiguities.description: Earlier chapters contain unverified claims about Alistair knowingly sacrificing Oakhaven, seeing a void/truth beyond the false sky, seeking divine ascent, or directing the wider plan. Chapters 20–21 directly confirm that Alistair accepts sacrifice to maintain the Vòm Trời and wants Elena’s power for Solaria, but they do not yet confirm the earlier void/divine-ascent claims.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Upgrade only Alistair’s directly spoken sacrifice/maintenance position to canonical. Keep the void/false-sky backstory and divine-ascent interpretation unverified.

ambiguities.description: Chapter 18 directly establishes that the northern tunnel entrance collapses behind the refugees. Chapter 19 then narrates that Oakhaven itself has been completely buried under vast rockfall, a much larger destruction state not directly shown in chapter 18.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Treat the escape route/tunnel entrance as sealed. Do not use total burial/destruction of the entire village as high-confidence ground truth without later confirmation.

ambiguities.description: Chapter 20 describes only nineteen surviving Oakhaven lives at the north tower, while chapters 22, 26, and 29 refer to more than three hundred or roughly four hundred Oakhaven refugees. The source does not explain how the population increases by this scale.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Do not use a precise survivor count as benchmark ground truth across this span. Use only local chapter-specific counts when explicitly querying that chapter.

ambiguities.description: Chapter 20 introduces Alistair with the right arm already amputated/replaced by an ancient metal apparatus containing a Space Core fragment. Chapter 21 then depicts the spatial rupture severing his right arm area with fresh biological injury, and chapter 22 summarizes Alan as having cut off Alistair’s arm.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Canonicalize only that Alistair has a major right-arm injury/apparatus state and is severely damaged by the chapter-21 spatial rupture. Do not freeze the exact pre/post anatomy without human review.

ambiguities.description: Chapter 22 has Elena reunite with Brand, meet Bram, and establish an alliance at the route to the fourth forge. Chapter 23 then presents Elena as having spent two days and nights alone crossing the Răng Cưa area under pursuit, without explaining a departure from that group; chapter 25 later reunites her with Alan before they again head toward Bram.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Preserve each chapter’s local events but do not assume a clean elapsed-time sequence between chapters 22–25. Avoid using “two days alone” as a high-confidence global timeline fact.

ambiguities.description: Alistair explicitly crushes Alan’s ordinary iron short sword into pieces in chapter 20, yet chapters 23–25 again give Alan an ordinary iron short sword/its hilt without narrating acquisition of a replacement.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Treat the chapter-20 sword destruction as canonical and the later ordinary-sword identity as unresolved. Do not infer that the same destroyed weapon survived.

ambiguities.description: Alan and Elena remain separated through chapters 23–24, and chapter 25 stages their reunion near its end, but the opening of chapter 25 says Alan’s shoulder was “just stitched/treated by Elena,” implying treatment that could not have occurred in the shown sequence.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Do not use Elena’s pre-reunion treatment in chapter 25 as clean temporal ground truth. Treat their visible reunion later in chapter 25 as the reliable state transition.

ambiguities.description: Chapter 22 explicitly establishes the Oakhaven–Frostspine dwarf survival alliance through Elena’s offer to detoxify water in exchange for shelter. Chapter 26 repeats the same initial distrust, water-for-shelter bargain, proof, and acceptance as though the alliance were being created for the first time.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Use chapter 22 as the earlier alliance-establishment anchor. Treat chapter 26 as a replay/reaffirmation and exclude its “first establishment” framing from clean chronology benchmarks.

ambiguities.description: The newly forged Thần Tinh short sword is described as two and a half thước long in chapter 27 but as two thước two tấc in chapter 28; chapters 32, 33, 35, and 36 repeatedly use the two-thước-two-tấc measurement. The later repetition favors one reading but does not erase the explicit chapter-27 conflict.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Canonicalize the object and its anti-mana function, but not its exact length until reviewed.

ambiguities.description: Chapter 21 first identifies Elena as possessing a Bản Nguyên Tịnh Hóa important to Solaria, while earlier chapters primarily frame her methods as non-mana medicine/chemistry; chapter 23 says this power is fully blocked. Its origin, prior availability, and exact mechanics are not explained in the processed source.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: It is canonical that Alistair names this power and chapter 23 says it is blocked. Do not infer its full mechanics or prior usage history.

ambiguities.description: Chapter 27 forges Alan’s first Thần Tinh sword and chapters 28–29 use it in combat. Chapters 31–32 then repeat the setup “obtain Thần Tinh ore → forge the first anti-Temple short sword” as though the weapon did not already exist.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Use chapter 27 as the clean origin anchor because the sword is demonstrably present in chapters 28–29. Retain chapter 32 as an explicit source event but mark its first-forging framing as narrative replay and a hard negative for object-history retrieval.

ambiguities.description: Korgan and Valora state that twelve auxiliary Pressure Pillars are deployed around the Frostspine/Hẻm Vực campaign, while chapters 32–33 repeatedly describe six devices/pillars in language that can read as the campaign total rather than an explicit subset.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Do not use an exact total pillar count as cross-chapter ground truth. It is safe to state that multiple auxiliary pillars exist and that Pillar No. 1 is destroyed in chapter 34.

ambiguities.description: Chapter 30 says Brand and Bram are separated from Alan/Elena at the collapsed fourth forge and retreat through maintenance chambers. Chapter 32 places Bram at the ancient-tomb forge and Brand later arrives there, but their route/reunion with the new alliance is not narrated.
ambiguities.ground_truth_policy: Treat their explicit presence in chapter 32 as canonical local state, but do not invent the missing travel/reunion sequence or timing.

open_questions.question: What is the reliable fate of Miller and Jory?
How should chapter 10 be ordered relative to the chapter-9 refuge ending?
Are Thánh Đô and Solaria the same location, and are Tòa Thánh and Thần Điện strict aliases or distinct institutional layers?
Is the blacksmith Miller the same person as the scout Miller introduced earlier?

Alistair now directly confirms willingness to sacrifice Oakhaven to maintain the Vòm Trời and use Elena for Solaria; are the earlier Varian-attributed claims about the void/false sky and Alistair seeking divine ascent ever directly confirmed?
Was all of Oakhaven physically buried/destroyed, or only the northern escape entrance sealed?
What is the reliable Oakhaven survivor count after the north-tower escape?
What is the exact continuity of Alistair’s right arm and the Mảnh Lõi Không Gian across chapters 20–22?
How should chapters 22–26 be ordered around Elena’s time alone, reunion with Alan, and the repeated dwarf-alliance bargain?
What are the origin and exact mechanics of Elena’s Bản Nguyên Tịnh Hóa, and why was it not previously foregrounded?
How should the repeated Thần Tinh first-forging scene in chapter 32 be reconciled with the chapter-27 forge and chapter-28/29 combat use?
Is the intended auxiliary Pressure Pillar total twelve, six, or six as a subset of twelve?
What exactly is the Mảnh Lõi Sinh Mệnh, how do the characters know it is in the lower tomb, and what function will it have?
How did Brand and Bram move from the collapsed fourth forge to the ancient-tomb alliance/forge between chapters 30 and 32?
